semantics.note: Faithful. The 'would suggest' inference and the Oracle share are kept as hedged. The checkable part is what OpenAI said and whether it defined the measure.

contract.note: Fair plain reading: did OpenAI give about 1.9 GW and leave the measure undefined? The hedged Microsoft/Oracle inference is rightly left unscored. The timing wording (Jan 2026 post about 2025) does not change the result.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own post (Jan 18, 2026) gives ~1.9 GW for 2025 and calls it 'available compute' without saying whether it means power drawn, IT load or energized capacity. As the source of the claim being described, it is the right evidence.

reviews.rationale: OpenAI's post gives ~1.9 GW of compute for 2025 and never says what the GW figure measures. The word 'available' hints at accessibility but does not define it, so the contradiction condition (a clear definition) is not met. The hedged Microsoft/Oracle inference is not scored.
